generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the herb base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the herb program gave as defaults until then.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 421: calyx and corolla of 3 to 5 lobes; Floral Diagrams p. 328 general formula: 4 to 5 (Veronica and Plantago 4, Penstemon 5).

traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 421, 505: Simpson calls the flowers hypogynous or epigynous. Simpson p. 505 defines hypogynous and epigynous as flowers without a hypanthium.

traits.note: The Lucid key to the flowering plant families, with Reed College's family page, as search results quote them (the pages themselves were not read): corolla sympetalous, usually 4- or 5-lobed, often two-lipped (regular in Plantago); stamens 4 (didynamous) or 2, on the corolla tube; ovary superior, of 2 carpels, one style.

traits.stipules.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), families 324 Scrophulariaceae (in part: foxgloves, speedwells, snapdragons, beardtongues) and 297 Plantaginaceae (plantains), which APG joins as Plantaginaceae: herbs or shrubs; leaves alternate, opposite or whorled; stipules absent; fruit a capsule, in the plantains opening by a lid.

traits.woodiness.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), families 324 Scrophulariaceae (in part: foxgloves, speedwells, snapdragons, beardtongues) and 297 Plantaginaceae (plantains), which APG joins as Plantaginaceae: herbs or shrubs; leaves alternate, opposite or whorled; stipules absent; fruit a capsule, in the plantains opening by a lid.

traits.fruit_type.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), families 324 Scrophulariaceae (in part: foxgloves, speedwells, snapdragons, beardtongues) and 297 Plantaginaceae (plantains), which APG joins as Plantaginaceae: herbs or shrubs; leaves alternate, opposite or whorled; stipules absent; fruit a capsule, in the plantains opening by a lid. The books add schizocarp (sometimes), berry (sometimes), achene (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 421, 423, 424: capsule, achene, berry or schizocarp.

traits.rosette.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Plantaginaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Globulariaceae, Hippuridaceae: whether the leaves gather in rosettes (character 22), coded often a basal rosette, often no rosette. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.life_span.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Plantaginaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Globulariaceae, Hippuridaceae: the herbs' life form (character 21), coded often annual, often biennial, often perennial. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.leaf_division.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Plantaginaceae with Globulariaceae and Hippuridaceae, which APG and WCVP join to it (their extra states read as sometimes): leaves simple; the simple blade none usually, lobed sometimes; lobes or leaflets pinnate. Read from the coded leaf form and dissection by script (spec-rework/b1/delta). Watson and Dallwitz's Plantaginaceae is Plantago alone; APG's family also takes in Veronica, Penstemon, Antirrhinum and their kin from the old Scrophulariaceae, whose leaves are simple and mostly unlobed (toothed or entire), so the reading stands for them (inferred, not traced).

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 421, 423, 424, family Plantaginaceae: leaf arrangement spiral, opposite or whorled; read as {"alternate": "often", "opposite": "often", "whorled": "often"}.

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 421, 423, 424, family Plantaginaceae: inflorescence head, raceme, thyrse or solitary; read as {"head": "often", "panicle": "often", "raceme": "often", "solitary": "often"}.

traits.ovary_position.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add inferior (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 421, 423, 424: superior or inferior.

traits.carpels.note: Rare extremes noted only; the count's source is the family's `traits` note. The books give the family low 1: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 421, 423, 424: 1-2. Left out of the range on the owner's go (2026-10-15): they belong to some of its genera, and a family's rare ends would reach every species that inherits its count.

traits.stamens.note: Rare extremes noted only; the count's source is the family's `traits` note. The books give the family low 1 and high 8: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 421, 423, 424: 1-8. Left out of the range on the owner's go (2026-10-15): they belong to some of its genera, and a family's rare ends would reach every species that inherits its count.
